namedSceneBlocker: The keeper's council offering gesture used separate rigid upper/lower sleeves, opening the garment silhouette at the elbow. A connected sleeve is needed before a final clothed performance.

source.rights: New deterministic sleeve geometry is SHI-authored. Existing body, rig and materials retain their recorded source provenance; no new model, texture, mocap or third-party clothing was used.
source.character: keeper; existing blockout retained. This is not the photorealistic Chen Sheng face used in the rain image.
source.preserved: Source file hash, body vertex basis and skin weights, all 53 bone matrices over 121 source frames, and existing palm gesture. No accepted asset, runtime export or narrative definition replaced.

implementation.method: 600 vertices and 576 quads per connected open sleeve; rounded centerline and tangent, normalized upper/lower-arm weights with smooth transition, volume-preserving armature deformation. Existing rigid sleeves retained hidden in the editable study.
implementation.simulation: No cloth simulation or physical material strain model.

verification.topology: One connected surface and two open 24-vertex boundary loops per sleeve. No collapsed faces; weights sum to one.
verification.rejectedFirstAttempt: Normals were rounded around a sharp centerline, producing near-coincident inner elbow rows and a 6.42058 maximum edge change factor. Rounded centerline revision reduced it to 1.96711.
verification.scope: Body clearance samples vertices and face centers over the full source interval. They do not prove exact triangle collision, cloth self-collision, physical strain or natural acting. Shoulder/armpit attachment remains red, with 64.86 mm sampled penetration; it was not omitted from the global result.

render.format: 1280x720, 30 fps, 120 H.264 frames, four seconds, silent
render.review: Agent inspected initial/peak/return poses and movie frames 27 and 120. Full movie decode passed. Diagnostic arm/torso framing intentionally crops the head; no human normal-speed viewing or cinematic acting acceptance claimed.

remaining: Fit the sleeve shoulder/armpit join to the torso garment and review body intersections without hiding the measured problem.
Develop believable cloth shape and folds; nearly twofold local edge changes do not establish physical fabric quality.
Review natural timing, fingers, full costume, identity and actual scene staging before replacing any game footage.
Keep this as named-scene engineering evidence, not finished game content.
